name: MangDang Mini Pupper 2 Pro
description: A 12-DOF quadruped robot dog kit running full ROS2 on a Raspberry Pi 4/CM4, descended from Stanford Student Robotics' open-source "Stanford Pupper" research platform. The Pro tier upgrades to servos with velocity and torque feedback, not just position, and pairs with an optional spinning lidar for genuine SLAM/Nav2 navigation — a step up in compute and software depth from this catalog's Petoi Bittle X, at roughly double the price once add-ons are included.

sourcing: Verified against MangDang's official Mini Pupper 2 Pro and Mini Pupper 2 product pages, its "About Us" page, and both Kickstarter campaign pages (2021 original, 2022 Mini Pupper 2); the mangdangroboticsclub/QuadrupedRobot and mini_pupper_ros GitHub repositories and their license/star counts; the peer-reviewed Stanford Pupper paper (arXiv:2110.00736) and Stanford Student Robotics' own project page; the LDROBOT STL-06P lidar datasheet; the Raspberry Pi Official Magazine's independent review; and IEEE Spectrum's 2022 robot gift guide entry. Flagged as uncertain: exact battery runtime in minutes (not officially published by MangDang); the Mini Pupper 2 Pro Maker Kit's current availability, shown sold out directly from MangDang at research time; and the extent of independent peer-reviewed citation of MangDang's specific commercial kit, as opposed to the underlying Stanford Pupper research it's derived from.

pricing.summary: The Mini Pupper 2 Pro Maker Kit lists at $799, with MangDang's own store showing it discounted to $559 on promotion. At research time it was listed as sold out directly from MangDang, so buyers currently have to look to distributors such as RobotShop and OzRobotics.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: MangDang's core GitHub repo for Mini Pupper is genuinely open (MIT license, ~1,200 stars), with real if modest community activity — a legitimate open robotics project, not a large or fast-moving one.
